guarantees.claim: On reset (rst_ni low), alerts_q[1] is cleared to 0.
When rst_ni is high and alerts[1] is high, alerts_q[1] is set to 1 on the next positive edge of clk_i.
When rst_ni is high and alerts[1] is low, alerts_q[1] retains its previous value (sticky behavior).

assumptions.claim: alerts[1] must remain high for at least one clock cycle after reset deassertion in order to be captured.
assumptions.cond: when a fatal alert occurs near reset release
assumptions.risk: If alerts[1] deasserts before the first rising clk_i after reset release, the fatal alert is not latched.

assumptions.claim: No other process drives alerts_q[1] while rst_ni is high; only this block may set or clear it.
assumptions.risk: A concurrent write could clear or corrupt the sticky fatal alert register, violating the intended latching behavior.

uncertain_points.claim: If a fatal alert occurs during reset and deasserts before the first clock edge after reset release, the sticky bit may remain 0, missing a fatal event.
uncertain_points.cond: reset active and alert pulse duration shorter than the time to first post-reset clock edge
uncertain_points.risk: A fatal condition that should permanently set the alert register could be silently ignored, leading to a false sense of safety.
